CORAM : GAUTAM A. ANKHAD, J.
DATE : 22nd OCTOBER, 2026.
P.C. :
1. This Petition is filed seeking Legal Heirship Certificate under
Section 2 of Bombay Regulation (VIII) of 1827 in respect of the
Deceased – Kerba Gundappa Wharge also known as Keraba Gundappa
Vharage who at the time of his death was residing at Post : Kaneri,
Taluka : Panhala, District : Kolhapur – 416 230. The Deceased died
intestate on 21st October, 2017 and a copy of the death certificate is
annexed at Exhibit ‘A’ to the Petition.
2. The Petitioner is the only son and the only legal heir of the
Deceased. It is further stated that the parents and wife of the Deceased

have predeceased the Deceased and there are no other heirs and next-of-
kin of the Deceased. It is in this background that the Petitioner seeks the
Heirship Certificate.
3. The reasons for filing this Petition are stated at paragraph no.6 of
the Petition. It is also stated that the Petitioner has not filed any other
Petition for Heirship Certificate, Succession Certificate, Probate or
Letters of Administration and there is no impediment to the grant of the
reliefs in this Petition.
4. As far as the delay is concerned, the same is condoned in the light
of the judgment of this Court in Ganpati Vinayak Achwal 1 wherein this
Court has held that the right to apply is a continuous right which is
capable of being exercised at any time after the death of the Deceased,
as long as the right to do so exists.
5. In view of the statements/undertakings contained in the Petition,
which are accepted, Miscellaneous Petition No.1191 of 2026 is allowed
in terms of prayer clause (a), which reads as under :
(a) This Honble Court be pleased to declare that Shri
Santosh Kerba Wharge, the Son of the deceased, is

1. The petitioners and the State are represented by learned
Advocates.
2. On behalf of the petitioners, it is submitted that considering the
fact that only 26.065 kg of ganja was recovered from the joint
possession of the present three accused petitioners and also
considering the fact that investigation has already been
completed, the instant application for bail may be considered
favourably.
3. While opposing the prayer for bail learned Advocate appearing on
behalf of the respondent State draws attention of this Court to the
status report as submitted by the concerned SI. It is further
submitted that the present petitioners have so many criminal
antecedents.

[2]
4. On careful perusal of the entire materials as placed before this
Court, it appears that commercial quantity of contraband was
seized from the accused petitioners. It further appears that so
many criminal antecedents of similar such offences are there
against the present petitioners.
5. Considering the entire circumstances, prayer for bail is rejected.
6. Urgent photostat certified copy of the order, if applied for, be
given to the parties, upon usual undertakings.
(PARTHA SARATHI SEN, J.)
